Subject: Renewal summary + latency spike follow-ups

Hi Olga,

We're preparing for our annual renewal and I wanted to collect a short summary from your side with three things:

- Confirmed token spend for Q4 '27 and any obvious drivers for the ~27% month-over-month increase in December.
- Recent latency incidents — our app team saw a handful of 95th-percentile spikes on the chat route during peak PDT hours (Dec 12–15). Were these traced to model fallbacks / autoscaling?
- A concise ROI recap we can share with procurement that shows net cost vs. latency improvements if we move to the dedicated pool you mentioned earlier.

We have a renewal target for Feb 1 and I'd like to get this on paper (and loop in Mike from procurement) so we don't get rushed. Can you send a 1-page summary + any relevant attachments?

Thanks — Claire
Claire Huang
Director, Product Integrations
LumenHealth

Subject: Re: Renewal summary + latency spike follow-ups

Claire — thanks for the note and the heads-up on timing. I put together the baseline materials and a short plan for bridging to a renewed, dedicated configuration that addresses both cost predictability and the latency spikes you observed. See attachments: usage_report_q4_2027.csv and latency_benchmarks_q4_2027.pdf.

High level answers:
- Q4 token spend: total 1.14B tokens; December saw a 27% MoM increase driven by two items: (1) experimental expanded-context prompts rolled out to 10% of sessions (prompt length +30%) and (2) a transient integration loop that increased assistant prompts on certain webhooks (we flagged and patched 12/20). Full breakdown in usage_report_q4_2027.csv.
- Latency spikes: Root cause was autoscaling warmup + a temporary fallback to the 'stable-0901' family during a midnight model transfer. That produced a short-lived 95th percentile increase (averaged +220ms) between 12/12–12/15. Our serving logs show the fallback window and we included the timeline in latency_benchmarks_q4_2027.pdf.
- ROI for dedicated pool: three scenarios (summary below) — detailed calc in roi_snapshot_v2.xlsx.

Renewal options (short):
1) Conservative — Renew hosted with a 20% commit uplift, include 8h/day burst credits for peak hours. Estimated savings vs pay-as-you-go: ~12% annual.
2) Dedicated pilot — 3-month dedicated pilot (reserved N GPUs) + migration support; expected 95th latency improvement ~120–200ms for chat routes, unit cost drop ~18% after steady-state.
3) Full reserved — 12-month dedicated commit with priority routing and higher headroom; best unit economics (-26%).

Proposed next steps:
- Friday 1/13 — 30-min call to pick an option and confirm procurement contacts
- I will share a one-page summary + DocuSign for the preferred option after the call

Would Friday 1/13 10:00–10:30 PT work for you?

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
